_note: The one place a technique predicate is defined (docs/techniques/STANDARD.md 5). evaluation: auto = a field the tools emit today (survey_field set), manual = an agent judges from tool output and disassembly, proposed = no tool yet. Values per routine or figure class are true / false / unknown / conflicted, each with basis and scope.

render.composition.xor.means: every write the routine makes to its target (screen or buffer) is XOR of the byte read
render.composition.xor.true_when: every screen-writing instruction of the routine XORs the old byte (e.g. LD A,(DE) / XOR (HL) / LD (HL),A) over the stated scope
render.composition.xor.false_when: any write in scope is overwrite, OR or AND
render.composition.xor.probe: scan GAME.z80 --rzx R --range 0x4000-0x57FF --writers lists the writing PCs (it does not classify them); disassemble those PCs (PLAYBOOK 2)

render.target.back_buffer.means: the figure plotter draws into a RAM buffer that a separate routine copies to the screen
render.target.back_buffer.true_when: the plotter's writes land in a RAM range and a block copy (LDIR / LDI / PUSH) from that range writes the screen
render.target.back_buffer.false_when: the plotter writes the screen bitmap directly
render.target.back_buffer.probe: survey.md block-copy rows hint at it; scan GAME.z80 --rzx R --range BUF --writers on the copied range

render.unit.partial_image.means: one plot call draws less than a whole figure image (a row, slice, quarter) for at least one entry or effect
render.unit.partial_image.true_when: for some plot entry, the rows or bytes drawn per call are fewer than the figure's full graphic, in a state the recording reaches
render.unit.partial_image.false_when: every entry draws whole images over the stated scope (normal play and every effect reached)
render.unit.partial_image.probe: detect.tracked-unit: compare rows drawn per call with the graphic's height byte / row count, per entry and per effect

screen.gameplay_reads_figure_pixels.means: game logic (collision, landing, decisions) reads screen bytes that hold figure pixels, and the result depends on them
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_pixels.true_when: a non-drawing routine reads a byte holding figure pixels and its result changes if the figure is removed
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_pixels.false_when: every read of figure pixels in scope is a drawer's own read-modify-write
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_pixels.probe: detect.gameplay-screen-readers (no shared command yet; BRIEFING C2 candidate)

screen.other_writers_change_figure_bits.means: routines other than the figure plotters overwrite or modify bytes holding figure pixels (clears, boxes, scenery, text)
screen.other_writers_change_figure_bits.true_when: a writer other than the plotters changes a figure bit in scope
screen.other_writers_change_figure_bits.false_when: no other writer touches figure bits in scope
screen.other_writers_change_figure_bits.probe: scan GAME.z80 --rzx R --range 0x4000-0x57FF --writers, then classify each non-plotter writer against the figures' bytes

design.figures_in_front.means: the user's design answer puts converted figures in front of scenery
design.figures_in_front.true_when: the stage-1 answer (default 3 changed, or an exception) says figures go in front
design.figures_in_front.false_when: figures keep the game's own depth rule

exec.interrupts_on_at_sites.means: interrupts are enabled when the candidate hook sites run
exec.interrupts_on_at_sites.true_when: IFF is 1 at the site in any recorded call
exec.interrupts_on_at_sites.false_when: IFF is 0 at every recorded call and the code path shows DI before the site
exec.interrupts_on_at_sites.probe: isr GAME.z80 --rzx R (handler, slots, stack); a trace of IFF at the site

exec.isr_calls_routine.means: the game's interrupt handler calls (directly or indirectly) the routine being hooked
exec.isr_calls_routine.true_when: a call path from the ISR entry reaches the routine
exec.isr_calls_routine.false_when: no path from the ISR reaches it (static) and none is seen in the recording
exec.isr_calls_routine.probe: isr GAME.z80 --rzx R for the handler; survey callers of the routine with the interrupt marked

exec.routine_not_reentrant.means: the routine keeps state in fixed memory or self-modified code, so a nested call corrupts the outer one
exec.routine_not_reentrant.true_when: it writes globals or its own operands that it later reads within the same call
exec.routine_not_reentrant.false_when: all its working state is in registers or on the stack
exec.routine_not_reentrant.probe: disassemble the routine: list LD (nn),r / LD (nn),A writes into data or its own code, and their later reads

exec.isr_must_run_on_time.means: delaying the interrupt handler by a few thousand T changes behaviour (music timing, raster effects, frame counters read mid-frame)
exec.isr_must_run_on_time.true_when: the handler's work is timing-critical in a way a delay changes
exec.isr_must_run_on_time.false_when: the handler's work tolerates running later in the same frame
exec.isr_must_run_on_time.probe: isr GAME.z80 --rzx R; read what the handler does; ask the user if music or effects are involved

hook.adds_time.means: the hooks add enough T-states to move later code relative to the interrupt
hook.adds_time.true_when: hook cost per frame is non-trivial against the gap the original leaves before the interrupt
hook.adds_time.false_when: hooks add no time on the path (pure data patches)
hook.adds_time.probe: no shared hook-cost tool (BRIEFING C2 #1); measure T per frame in the verifier's pair runs

hook.updates_visible_image.means: a hook changes what a visible sprite or layer shows while the original routine is still drawing
hook.updates_visible_image.true_when: the hook writes sprite attributes, patterns or Layer 2 that are on screen during the plot
hook.updates_visible_image.false_when: replacement graphics change only while hidden or at a point the beam cannot show mid-update
hook.updates_visible_image.probe: read the hook design; cost GAME.z80 --rzx R --at PLOTTER gives how long a plot runs

plot.call_target_redirectable.means: the plotters get their destination from a shared helper or CALL target that a hook can replace without changing their loops
plot.call_target_redirectable.true_when: every converted plotter obtains its buffer address from one CALL / helper whose return value can be redirected
plot.call_target_redirectable.false_when: destinations are computed inline in each plotter
plot.call_target_redirectable.probe: disassemble each plotter's entry; list CALLs shared between them

mem.hook_page_slot_free.means: a Next MMU slot exists that the ISR never touches, so a hook can map its own page there while interrupts are on
mem.hook_page_slot_free.true_when: the full-RZX isr slot scan shows the slot untouched by the handler (and its paging writes)
mem.hook_page_slot_free.false_when: the handler touches every candidate slot

sprite.working_set_fits.means: the distinct images shown at once fit in pattern memory (or the planned cache) in the worst scene
sprite.working_set_fits.true_when: distinct images per worst frame fit the cache entries / pattern slots planned
sprite.working_set_fits.false_when: the worst recorded scene needs more distinct images than the cache holds
sprite.working_set_fits.probe: cost GAME.z80 --rzx R --at PLOTTER --group IX; count distinct graphics per frame in the worst scene

render.paints_figure_attributes.means: the figure plotter writes the attribute cells under the figure (its colour), so scenery around it changes colour (clash)
render.paints_figure_attributes.true_when: a plotter instruction writes 0x5800-0x5AFF in scope
render.paints_figure_attributes.false_when: the plotters never write attributes in scope
render.paints_figure_attributes.probe: scan GAME.z80 --rzx R --range 0x5800-0x5AFF --writers: plotter PCs among the writers

screen.gameplay_reads_figure_attributes.means: game logic reads attribute cells the plotter painted, and the result depends on the painted value
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_attributes.true_when: a non-plotter instruction reads an attribute cell after a plotter painted it, in scope
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_attributes.false_when: no reader of painted cells in scope (unreached paths listed as unknowns)
screen.gameplay_reads_figure_attributes.probe: scan GAME.z80 --rzx R --range 0x5800-0x5AFF --writers (readers), then painted-cell tracking per reader

design.no_figure_clash.means: the user's design answer keeps the scenery's colours under and around converted figures
design.no_figure_clash.true_when: the design answer (or a later round) asks for no clash on the scenery
design.no_figure_clash.false_when: the clash halo of the original is kept
design.no_figure_clash.probe: the design question (PLAYBOOK 3c) or a hardware-round report

sprite.patterns_built_at_runtime.means: the hooks convert the game graphics into sprite patterns at run time (at the draw), so the build has no pattern per image to colour
sprite.patterns_built_at_runtime.true_when: the pattern code reads the graphic from game memory inside a hook (Cauldron: upload builds a canvas + outline per draw)
sprite.patterns_built_at_runtime.false_when: patterns are prepared at build time from a known image list (Dizzy 1 plane, Midnight Resistance commits)
sprite.patterns_built_at_runtime.probe: read the engine design: where the pattern bytes (port 0x5B) come from
